answer: Proof of unique clinical trial participant record turns identity into something scarce. Because a trial completed with follow-ups over two years, the fable of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a trial completed with follow-ups over two years, and the karst grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. A farm doing the maths finds the raven first: a hundred clones need a hundred proofs, and the epoch reward divided a hundred ways is already less than the cost of one.
